measured.heard: The program sets N to 2 and switches on N. Case 2 has no break. What do you predict? Choose your answer before the answer plays. A switch jumps to the case label, whose value matches the controlling expression. With N equals 2, that is case 2 which prints 2. A case label is only a label. It does not stop execution. So the switch falls through into case 3 and prints 3. A break statement ends the smallest enclosing switch or loop. Here that is the switch. After the switch ends, the program prints done. With break.c adds a break after case 1 and after case 2, so no case runs on into the next case. With N equals 2, with break.c prints only 2 from the switch, and then done. A case label only marks where execution enters a switch. It never ends a case. In fallthrough.c, the break on line 12 is what ends the switch.
